analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/reference/configuration.md (date bump to 2026-10-31 and an expanded 'Cluster runtime facts' section, head lines ~923-1008, plus a 'Coordinator-paired member' wording tweak at ~1070-1076). No code, controls, defaults or endpoints change in the supplied evidence. Cache env-var table (lines 684-698) is unchanged context and consistent with T-041 (30-minute TTL max, DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch, debug key file DEBUG-only, test-root gated on ALLOW_EPHEMERAL); I saw no drift that weakens those statements.

The new text describes how a signed release registers `cluster_runtime` via POST /v1/releases and how the coordinator derives approvals, pair-serving grants and parity qualifications from it. It also states that public GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-27B traffic is admitted on any Apple silicon pair within the request envelope, on the owner's decision and DevNet results rather than cross-cable or M5 Ultra pipeline runs (lines ~976-995). This is a coordinator-side policy claim owned by darkbloom-platform, so it is a documented policy choice rather than a provider regression. It touches A-017/A-011-style release-trust concepts and TB-002, but the implementation is outside the supplied evidence: the coordinator's release-registration auth, the `parityQualification` behavior (pinned link to df61dd6f...) and scripts/provider-release-publication.py were not provided. The hunk text for lines 958-995 and the strict-decoder rules at 997-1008 describe controls (canonical form, ID length limits, strict unknown-field rejection) whose enforcement was not reviewed. Threat-model note: if the platform treats cluster_runtime in release registration as a new trust input, the platform threat model, not this provider one, should record it. No finding is raised because no concrete regression in supplied code is visible. Remaining question for integration: confirm the platform-side release-registration authentication (A-005) covers the new cluster_runtime block.
